subject: Audit log extract process, immutability guarantees, and next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Reed <marcus.reed@wellnesscorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Audit log extract process, immutability guarantees, and next steps

Hi Lydia and Marcus,

Thanks again for taking the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture.

Summary of what WellnessCorp asked about on the call:
- Full admin activity and API request logs for production accounts (audit events, who/when/what).
- Ability to export logs in a tamper-evident format for incident forensics and retention.
- Controls for immutability (write-once/read-many or signed manifests) and chain-of-custody to satisfy your internal compliance and auditors.

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Export endpoints that produce NDJSON batches with event metadata and per-batch SHA256 manifests.
- S3-friendly delivery (pre-signed upload or push to your bucket) and a signed manifest file containing checksums and export timestamps.
- Optional time-based snapshots and WORM-compatible packaging using our export service + a signed manifest for integrity proofs.
- Admin UI to request exports, plus a Service Account API for scripted retrieval.

Open questions we need from you to scope the PoC:
1) Which event types are required in the initial export (admin_acl_change, api_request, model_deploy, key_rotation, audit_config_change)?
2) Retention window for the exported snapshots (30/90/365 days)?
3) Do you need HSM/KMS signing of manifests on your side or is Redwood-signed manifests acceptable for the first PoC?
4) Desired delivery mechanism: push to your S3 vs. pull from our presigned export endpoint?

Proposed immediate next steps (tentative timeline):
- Wed 2027-06-16: Technical working session with your security engineer to finalize event scope and delivery method. (30–45m)
- Fri 2027-06-18: Provide sample export (1 day window, 1GB cap) for verification — includes manifest and verification script.
- Week of 2027-06-21: Sprint to add any required event payload fields and immutability tweaks.

I've attached a short data dictionary and a diagram showing the export flow. Marissa will follow up with an export checklist and the verification script.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers so you can scope the PoC: 

- Event types: priority 1: admin_acl_change, api_request, model_deploy, and auth_failure. Priority 2: key_rotation and config change events.
- Retention: We need exports that cover 365 days for audits, but for the PoC 30 days is fine.
- Manifest signing: For the PoC Redwood-signed manifests are acceptable, but long term we want either Redwood to push signed artifacts into our KMS-backed bucket or provide a manifest that we can sign with our HSM.
- Delivery: Push to our S3 preferred; we'll provide a dedicated export bucket with cross-account role.

Marcus will join the technical session on Wed. Can you include a quick note on how immutability is achieved (WORM vs signed manifests vs S3 object lock)? Our auditors will want that detail.

Best,
Lydia Park

Subject: Re: Audit log extract process, immutability guarantees, and next steps

Hi Lydia — following up with the technical detail you asked for ahead of Wednesday. Quick bullet answers and a short verification plan attached.

How we provide immutability and tamper evidence:
- Signed manifests: Each export chunk (hourly/daily, configurable) is accompanied by a manifest containing chunk SHA256 checksums, object list, export window, and a Redwood signature (ECDSA-SHA256). The manifest itself can be delivered to you and verified independently.
- S3 delivery options:
  * Push to customer S3 using cross-account role (recommended for PoC) — can be written with Object Lock retention mode if you enable governance/compliance mode on your bucket.
  * Pre-signed URLs for pull-based retrieval if cross-account roles are not allowed.
- WORM vs signatures: WORM (S3 Object Lock in compliance mode) is the strongest guarantee but requires bucket-side configuration and governance. Signed manifests + checksums provide cryptographic tamper-evidence without relying on bucket settings.
- Chain-of-custody: Export metadata includes exporter job id, initiating user/service account, and operation timestamps. All export operations are recorded in our internal admin audit table and included in the export as metadata.

Verification plan for the PoC sample export:
1) Redwood will produce a 24-hour sample (NDJSON) containing the agreed event types and a manifest.
2) We will push the files to your export bucket: s3://wellnesscorp-audit-exports/poc/2027-06-16/
3) You run our verification script (attached) to validate checksums and signature.
4) You confirm payload fields, timestamps, and retention semantics.

Attachments sent: immutability-briefing.txt, verification-script.sh
